J1.text: D2: where Narra's meaning differs from TypeScript's, Narra uses different syntax or an error with a fix; the same text never means two things. SPEC section 2 already lists `enum` as a known difference (TS: named numbers or strings; Narra: variants with fields).

J2.text: TypeScript enum text mostly keeps its meaning in Narra: `enum Color { Red, Green }` compiles as fieldless constructors, read as Color.Red after the qualified-constructor debate. `Red = 1` is a parse error ('expected a name, found "="') with no fix.

J3.text: In TypeScript, `type Shape = Circle | Square` is a union of existing types Circle and Square. Under the proposal, the same text would declare two new constructors named Circle and Square. Today it is a parse error.

evidence.source: narra run evidence/tsunion.nra; TS handbook (union types)

J4.text: `type A = B` already means an alias (SPEC section 3) and `distinct type A = B` a new nominal type. The proposal makes `type` declare a nominal sum type when the right side starts with `|`.

J5.text: Prior art: Rust, Swift, Haxe and Kotlin (enum class / sealed) use `enum` for sums with payloads. OCaml, F#, Haskell, Elm, Gleam and ReScript use `type ... = | A | B`. ReScript targets JS users with ML syntax throughout, not TS syntax.

J6.text: 68 enum declarations across selfhost and compiler/testdata; `enum` is parsed at parser.go:196/402 and in selfhost/src/parser.nra. Also `@repr(u8) enum` (SPEC section 12) and `derives` refer to enums.

J7.text: The previous debate settled qualified access, SchoolPerson.Teacher, which is exactly how TypeScript reads enum members.

P1.text: Declare sum types as `type SchoolPerson = | Teacher | Director | Student(name: string)` and drop the `enum` keyword. Semantics stay the same.

P2.text: By D2's own rule `enum` is the wrong word: TS enums are named constants, Narra enums are tagged unions, and SPEC already has to call this out.

P3.text: One declaration word (`type`) for aliases, distinct types and sums reads uniformly.

O1.text: TypeScript users and models will write `type Shape = Circle | Square` meaning a union of their structs, and get new constructors that shadow or clash with those struct names instead.

O2.text: 68 declarations, two parsers, SPEC, @repr and derives text change. Mechanical, but it lands in the same selfhost files as the constructor migration.

O3.text: Keep `enum`. Fix the one TS-habit gap J2 found: `Red = 1` should get an error whose fix points to @repr and Enum.fromInt.
